newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds close slightly lower.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds close slightly lower.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed slightly lower on Wednesday on relatively strong demand for CPI-linked bonds as traders braced for a further tightening of supply, traders said.
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.02 pct to 105.68
Volume including Makams was a very high 215 million shekels.

"There was demand of 105 million shekels for CPI-linked bonds today," said Gidi Halpern of Meitav Investments and Securities. "Demand was up for two reasons: Yields are at 4.2 percent, and it appears the government will meet its privatisation target, which will mean fewer debt issues."

Finance Minister Dan Meridor said on Tuesday that the successful completion of the Bank Leumi offering ensured that the government could meet its revenue target of three billion shekels from bank privatisations this year, not counting the proceeds from a tender offer now under way for a controlling stake in Bank Hapoalim.
If so, this will make it easier for the Treasury to keep to its revenue forecasts for the year.

Prices of CPI-linked bonds had been falling on expectations of lower inflation in the coming months and lower interest rates. An increasingly tight supply of CPI-linked bonds had kept the prices from falling even further, said one trader.

She said prices were also under pressure from investors cashing in bonds in order to move money into equities, particularly new issues. The Leumi offering, which was for $150 million, is only the biggest of a slew of new issues now taking place.
"The market was very mixed," said a trader. "People are starting to move money to the equity market."

Trading in Makams was mixed. "On one hand yields are at a high 13.87 percent causing people to buy. On the other hand, people are selling Makams to invest the money in the equity market," said Halpern.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
